sammendrag: In February 1998, the United Kingdom (UK) government issued 'The learning age: a renaissance for a new Britain' (indexed at TD/IRD 88.177), a Green Paper on lifelong learning which initiated the national Individual Learning Accounts (ILAs) scheme. The key objective of this scheme was to provide a vehicle for funding continuous learning. As part of the first year of the national ILAs scheme, the home countries required an early evaluation of the characteristics of ILA users and non-redeemers, the process and customer satisfaction. This is one of two reports prepared for publication. It summarises key similarities and differences between each of the four home countries (England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland) and is structured as follows: the first section provides background information on ILAs and the evaluation; section two outlines the methodology; section three presents the key findings based mainly on the responses of people who had redeemed their ILAs; section four covers accessing and using an ILA; section five contains feedback from course providers; section six lists the key conclusions emerging from this survey under the headings of Demographics, Target groups, Promotion, Prior learning, Administration of Individual Learning Accounts, Learning supported by Individual Learning Accounts, Learner/employer contributions, and Deadweight; and the final section sets out recommendations for each of the four countries. Also included as appendices are: ILA user/non redeemer questionnaire; Course provider questionnaires, Social class definitions; Opt-out letters; Methodology.
tittel: Evaluation of individual learning accounts: early views of customers & providers: national study
